answer: Bind each voting seat to a certified organic farm. A USDA-accredited certifier inspects the land every year, audits seed and input records, and lists the operation in a public directory, so each seat hangs by a thread to one inspected field. Even a wildflower meadow grown as nectar for local bees needs three years free of synthetic chemicals before it qualifies. Fees and inspections run about $2,500 per farm, so 1,000 sybil seats would cost an attacker roughly $2.5M, plus three years of waiting.
